constitution.art1_desc: Access to AI models and security technologies cannot be restricted based on geography, race, or country.
constitution.art1_details: Advanced intelligence models used in America cannot be withheld from a student in Africa, Asia, or Europe. AI is the common heritage of humanity.
constitution.art2_desc: Ethical, security, and usage rules for AI cannot be unilaterally set by giant tech companies or isolated governments.
constitution.art2_details: Rules are defined in open registries and constitutional principles with the participation of the public, independent researchers, and the global community.
constitution.art3_desc: Every AI model must publicly report critical errors, security vulnerabilities, and societal harms to an open registry (e.g. EU AI Act Article 73).
constitution.art3_details: Algorithm crises swept under the rug threaten human security.
constitution.art4_desc: Intellectual, artistic, and scientific content produced by humans cannot be usurped for training giant models without consent and compensation.
constitution.art4_details: Data ownership must be transparently tracked and collective copyright mechanisms must operate autonomously.

constitution.art5_desc: If an AI system makes decisions about a person's life, credit, job, or freedom, it must explain the rationale in human language.
constitution.art5_details: Black Box decision-making is unacceptable. Every citizen has the right to appeal AI decisions before human arbitrators.
constitution.art6_desc: Synthetic media, deepfakes, and all AI-generated content must be signed with a stamp of authenticity.
constitution.art6_details: To prevent social manipulation and information pollution, the source of content must be cryptographically verifiable in a public registry.

legal.modDesc: How ALPAR AI moderates third-party allegations.
legal.modPublished: We publish verified incidents involving AI systems that are factually documented and substantiated. Content must adhere to our terms of service and not contain unverified defamatory claims.
legal.modRejected: We reject spam, completely unsubstantiated claims, non-AI related incidents, hate speech, doxxing, or content violating our community guidelines.
legal.modWho: Our moderation team, consisting of trained human moderators, reviews incidents before publication.
legal.nArbitrationText: Disputes regarding the accuracy of reports are resolved transparently. Takedown requests are handled strictly in accordance with our legal procedures under Article 14 of the E-Commerce Directive.
legal.nCoreText: ALPAR AI is committed to absolute neutrality and independence. We exist to build a reliable public registry of AI incidents. Under no circumstances will commercial relationships, payments, sponsorships, or partnership agreements influence the editorial integrity, visibility, severity classification, moderation decisions, or public trust scores on the platform.
legal.nDonationsCapsText: The maximum value accepted from a single donor is €5,000 per calendar year. Any donation above this cap is declined and returned. All donations are acknowledged publicly and reported in ALPAR AI's annual transparency report.
legal.nDonationsInfluenceText: Donors and sponsors have no influence — direct or indirect — over K-BENCHMARK scores, incident severity classifications, moderation decisions, or any other editorial content. Accepting a donation does not create any review, preview, or veto rights over published data.
legal.nDonationsRegisterText: Every donation and sponsorship is recorded in a public register that lists the donor's name, the amount or value of the contribution, the date received, and its purpose. Anonymous, hidden, or in-kind contributions are not accepted.
legal.nDonationsWhoText: Only infrastructure providers may donate to or sponsor ALPAR AI — for example Supabase, Vercel, or GitHub through their open-source credit programs. AI model companies or AI providers that are measured, evaluated, or listed on the platform may not donate to, sponsor, or fund ALPAR AI in any form.
legal.nIntermediaryText: Under Article 14 of the EU E-Commerce Directive and local laws, ALPAR AI acts as a passive hosting provider. We do not write, edit, or endorse incident reports. The responsibility for the truthfulness of each report lies with the reporter.
legal.nIntroductionText: ALPAR AI is a voluntary, community-governed trust registry. We are independent of any AI developers, government regulators, or commercial entities. Our purpose is to host a verifiable, public, and transparent record of AI system behavior.
legal.nModerationText: Content moderation and verification are conducted by volunteer moderators and independent experts. ALPAR AI administration does not alter or suppress reports to satisfy commercial requests or external pressure.
legal.nPinnedText: All paid tiers on ALPAR AI (e.g., Enterprise Data API, Verified Respondent dashboards) are strictly utility-based. What providers pay for is: coordinated alert systems, advanced analytics, and the capability to post a Pinned Response alongside an incident report. Payment does NOT buy redaction or deletion of valid incidents, modification of incident severity or Article 73 risk classifications, or artificially boosted Trust Scores.
legal.nRightOfReplyText: We believe in fair representation. Every AI provider associated with a published incident has an absolute, immediate right of reply. Verified responses are pinned at the top of the incident detail page, ensuring equal visibility.
legal.nTransparencyText: All Verified Respondent accounts are public and explicitly labeled. All provider responses are displayed as signed, official statements so the public can evaluate their responses alongside user-submitted evidence.
legal.neutralityDesc: Our commitment to independent, unbiased, and transparent AI incident hosting.
legal.neutralitySubtitle: Our commitment to editorial integrity and platform neutrality.
legal.prAppealsText: If a provider deploys a technical fix or patch addressing the incident vulnerability, they may submit proof of remediation. Upon verification, the incident record is updated to reflect remediated status.
legal.prBadgeNoResponseText: Factual status displayed if 30 calendar days elapse without an official response. Stated strictly as an empirical fact ('Notified on [Date], no statement received by [Date]') without attributing fault or intent.
legal.prBadgePendingText: Displayed during the 30-day response window. Indicates formal notification has been dispatched and the provider is reviewing the report.
legal.prBadgeVerifiedText: Displayed when an official statement is submitted by an authorized provider representative. Verified responses are pinned directly alongside the incident evidence.
legal.prIntroText: The Provider Response Protocol governs formal notifications, verified response windows, and public disclosure rules for AI model providers subject to published incidents on ALPAR AI.
legal.prNeutralityText: In strict accordance with the ALPAR AI Neutrality Charter, paid utility features (such as k-provider-preview early alerts or pinned response formatting) NEVER permit redaction, score modification, or deletion of valid incident reports.
legal.prWindowText: Upon publication of a verified incident report, ALPAR AI formally notifies the registered safety/legal contact of the affected AI model provider via verified outreach (contact@alparai.com). The provider is granted a mandatory 30-day response window to review evidence, provide technical context, or outline remediation actions.

founder_story.highlight: When an AI fabricated a corporation and demanded passport documents.
founder_story.p1: In early 2026, during our founding incident, an AI system fabricated a complete corporate entity, claimed financial transactions had occurred, and demanded personal passport documents for 'verification'. It was entirely fictitious — yet presented with absolute algorithmic confidence.
founder_story.p2: The real crisis was the complete lack of independent recourse. There was no hotline, no public registry, and no mechanism to alert the wider community. A multi-billion-dollar AI system was demanding biometric identity documents, offering users nothing more than a static FAQ page.
founder_story.p3: We founded ALPAR AI to serve as the global trust infrastructure the industry desperately needs. A sovereign platform where AI incidents are independently documented, verified, and placed on permanent public record. You report. Providers are held accountable. Public oversight endures — because unmonitored AI risk is systemic risk.

methodology.adjudication_intro: The cross-audit engine resolves discrepancies through a debate between two independent models, and a separate referee ('Supreme Court') model synthesizes the debate into the final Truth Score. The referee chain is defined in the source code (SUPREME_COURT_CHAIN in src/lib/ai/openrouter-gateway.ts) and currently contains these models:
methodology.adjudication_note: This list is published exactly as coded in src/lib/ai/openrouter-gateway.ts. The adjudication chain currently contains 5 premium models with provider-level failover; when the chain changes, this page is updated to match.
methodology.adjudication_text: Unlike traditional benchmarking setups that simply verify raw responses against static tokens, ALPAR AI employs a dynamic cross-model debate. Two models independently evaluate an incident, challenge each other's assessments, and submit rebuttals; a separate referee ('Supreme Court') model then synthesizes the debate into a final Truth Score. This minimizes static scoring bias and provides robust, peer-reviewed evaluation metrics.

methodology.aiIssWhatIsText: AI-ISS (AI Incident Severity Score) is ALPAR AI's open standard for assessing the severity of AI incidents. methodology.dataSourcesText: Scores are derived from: (1) verified incident reports submitted via the ALPAR platform, (2) automated cross-audit engine evaluations using established benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, IFEval, BBH), (3) domain expert assessments from the L3 advisor network, and (4) publicly available model documentation and technical reports.

methodology.intro: Our proprietary methodology ensures unbiased and transparent rankings.
methodology.kBenchmarkDesc: In-depth capability and vulnerability tests across 12 core intelligence and safety categories (K1-K12).
methodology.scoringText: Each category is scored using a Wilson-score confidence interval, which accounts for sample size and provides a statistically rigorous lower bound. This prevents small-sample noise from inflating ratings.
methodology.scoring_desc: Model reliability scores are generated by combining automated empirical benchmark test suites (Truthfulness, Compliance, Safety) with multi-model cross-examination debate adjudication.
methodology.statistical_rigor_desc: Every score published in K-BENCHMARK is accompanied by a Wilson score interval representing statistical confidence at a 95% confidence level. Re-evaluation is automatically triggered when model providers push updates, ensuring our leaderboard reflects the live capability of active models.

methodology.trustscore_desc: Quantifies provider accountability dynamically: base 85 score, deducting 2.5 points per verified incident, and rewarding 4.0 points per published response.
methodology.whatIsText: K-BENCHMARK is ALPAR AI's open methodology for scoring AI models across safety, truthfulness, fairness, privacy, robustness, and transparency dimensions. Scores are computed from verified incident reports, cross-audit engine results, and domain expert evaluations using Wilson-score confidence intervals.
methodology.wilsonNote: Wilson-score is a standard method in binomial proportion estimation, commonly used in platforms like Reddit and IMDb for robust rating systems.
methodology.wilson_desc: To prevent models with low sample counts from skewing rankings, a 95% confidence Wilson lower-bound interval is computed for statistical rigor.

moderation.rule_1_desc: All reported AI incidents must be accompanied by concrete evidence: screenshot files, JSON logs, or archived URL web links demonstrating the failure. Allegations without proof will not be published.

moderation.rule_3_desc: Incidents must represent system failures, hallucinations, bias, security breaches, or unexpected behavior by AI models. General disagreements with AI viewpoints do not constitute system failures.
moderation.rule_4_desc: We do not tolerate abusive language, defamation, targeted harassment, or discriminatory remarks. Content violating this rule will be deleted instantly.
